notes: Samsung's spec table prints Folded/Unfolded as WIDTH x HEIGHT x DEPTH -- the second value is identical folded and unfolded (the hinge-axis dimension), so it is mapped to `height` and the first value to `width`. UNUSUAL FOR THIS FAMILY: the Fold8 is an all-new 'wider, shorter' form factor, so the hinge-axis dimension (123.9mm) is SHORTER than the unfolded across-hinge dimension (161.4mm) -- i.e. it opens into a LANDSCAPE 4:3 screen. `height` is therefore the hinge-axis dimension (constant in both states), not the longest edge; do not assume height > width when modelling. samsung.com/au corroborates the mapping in words: the Fold8 is 'wider, shorter and more pocket-friendly' than the Z Fold7 (72.8 x 158.4 folded), which matches 81.9 wide x 123.9 tall. Unfolded thickness footnote: 'does not include the frame of the Main Screen'. Single folded thickness -> depth_at_hinge null. Samsung's July 2026 press release does NOT list frame/back/cover-glass materials (no Armor Aluminum or Gorilla Glass wording anywhere in it) and the samsung.com/us spec page renders client-side and returned no text, so materials are null. Hinge is named 'Armor FlexHinge' (samsung.com/au) and the new 'Flex Titanium' display structure is said to 'reduce crease visibility', but no crease SHAPE is stated for this generation -> crease null. General availability is 2026-08-07 per Samsung's separate launch release (the Unpacked release itself mentions pre-order only). RESOLUTION ORDERING: recorded verbatim as Samsung prints it. Samsung is NOT consistent across generations -- the 2025 Z Fold7 table prints '(2184 x 1968)' and '(2520 x 1080, 21:9)' (long axis first) while the 2026 Z Fold8 / Fold8 Ultra table prints '(1,848 x 2,448)', '(1,248 x 1,972)' and '(1,080 x 2,520)' (short axis first). Do not assume a common [width,height] order. || EVIDENCE SWEEP 2026-09-13: these values were present in the research pass but carried NO sources[] entry covering their field, so they were set to null per the registry rule (a value without a citation is an assertion, not evidence).
